architecture.mechanism: Decoupling fuselage pitch attitude from wing angle of attack via variable-incidence aerodynamic surfaces to maintain optimal lift-to-drag performance across varying speeds.
architecture.intervention: Design a high-performance ground vehicle with active, variable-incidence aerodynamic surfaces (e.g., flaps, canards, or splitter adjustments) driven by lightweight actuators to independently optimize local AoA while keeping the vehicle body stable, thereby minimizing parasitic drag and rotor/airflow interference at extreme velocities.
architecture.expected_effect: Significant reduction in aerodynamic drag coefficients and powertrain energy losses at high speeds, resulting in increased terminal velocity and improved fuel/electricity efficiency while maintaining vehicle stability.
architecture.falsification_test: Test the vehicle in a wind tunnel or on a closed course at target extreme velocities; if the active variable-incidence system does not result in a measurable reduction in total drag force or a required power reduction of >5% compared to a fixed-geometry baseline while maintaining lateral stability, the mechanism is falsified.
